citations.B1: Read-modify-write on `counts` is not atomic across threads (get, compare, assign) — two threads can both see 99 and both allow
citations.B3: wrap the whole check-and-increment in a `threading.Lock`
citations.B4: No time window at all — counts accumulate forever, so every user is permanently blocked after 100 lifetime requests
citations.B5: `counts` never shrinks and is keyed by arbitrary caller-supplied `user_id` — unbounded memory growth
citations.B6: In-process dict guards one process only, so N workers each grant the full limit (N×100)
citations.B7: `user_id` is not validated or normalized — `None`, `""`, or case/whitespace variants become separate buckets
